comment: No source is published. The oscillator runs four channels at a time. Polyphony is real and not an isConnected test: the pitch jack's channel count is taken and used as the loop bound. The pitch knob is configured -48 to 48 with a display base of the twelfth root of two and a multiplier of 261.6256, so it is semitones around C4 and reads out in Hz; process divides it by twelve before adding the pitch jack. Rise and fall are each 0.025 to 0.2 of a cycle and are handed to the oscillator as the four corners of a trapezoid. The tilt, rise and fall jacks are read on channel 0 only and applied to every channel. The FM knob is squared with its sign kept, which is why small settings move the pitch so little. What the tilt control changes inside the oscillator beyond doubling into a 0 to 1 shape control was not traced further.
